title: Doggerland, the lost land under the North Sea
summary: Doggerland was a landmass in what is now the North Sea until rising seas in the mid-Holocene drowned it and separated Britain from the rest of Europe. About 8,150 years ago the Storegga submarine landslide off Norway sent a tsunami across the North Sea; deposits in the southern North Sea show its effects there were temporary and local, softened by woodland and terrain.

uncertainty.note: The Storegga slide failed "around 8150 years ago"; the wider inundation is dated only to the mid-Holocene.

beats.caption: About 8,150 years ago a submarine landslide off Norway set off the Storegga tsunami, which crossed the North Sea.
A tsunami deposit at the head of a buried river system in the southern North Sea shows the wave reached Doggerland.
The wave's effects there were temporary and local, softened by woodland and terrain; rising seas went on to cut Britain off from Europe.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the id-implied date of 10,000 BCE: the sources date only the Storegga tsunami (about 8,150 years ago) and the mid-Holocene inundation, so the record dates to the tsunami. Whether the tsunami emptied Doggerland is debated.
